title: 17th-century English herbal charms collection
publicDomainBasis: Originally compiled in the 1680s; this English-language edition is a pre-1930 transcription in the public domain in the United States.
summary: A collection of household charms built around common kitchen and garden herbs, used for protection, healing, and marking the turn of the seasons. Rituals are simple and tied to the hearth: herbs are gathered, dried, and spoken over at specific times of day, then kept near doorways or cookfires rather than consumed in large quantities.
